newsitem.title: USA: US securities group urges lawmakers enact reforms.
newsitem.headline: US securities group urges lawmakers enact reforms.

text.p: The Securities Industry Association said Tuesday it urged legislators to enact regulatory reforms before Congress adjourns later this year.

"It would be very regrettable if after months of hard work by Congress, this major legislation were to die in the home stretch because of unnecessary delays," SIA President Marc Lackritz and a number of its firms wrote in a letter.
SIA sent the letter dated August 29 to Senators Alfonse D'Amato (R-NY) and Paul Sarbanes (D-MD) and Representatives Thomas Bliley (R-VA) and John Dingell (D-MI).
The House and Senate both passed their versions of a securities bill before the August recess. Conference committee negotiations to reconcile differences between the two versions resume this week.
SIA said it urged the conferees to include provisions that would uniform federal standards in areas such as books and record requirements and uniform exemptions for secondary market trading.
"Allowing states to have additional requirements that are inconsistent with each other and with federal requirements simply adds unnecessary regulatory costs," the group said.
